name: Magna Carta Reissued 1216, Constitutional Permanence
summary: Following King John's death (1216), his nine-year-old son Henry III's regents issue a revised version of Magna Carta to win baronial support. Further revisions in 1217 (adding the Forest Charter) and 1225 (the definitive version) create the permanent constitutional framework. The 1225 version is entered into the English Statute Book and becomes the foundational law of England, cited in every subsequent constitutional crisis.

_quarry.structural_significance: Magna Carta's constitutional significance is created by these reissues rather than the 1215 original (which John immediately sought to annul); the 1225 version's permanent statutory status creates the precedent that the King of England is bound by law; the Forest Charter's provisions protecting common rights to woodland resources reflects how constitutional rights could extend beyond noble privileges to include common people's economic interests
